proof_skeleton_nl: Work in the localization-based congruence ring for the final modulus M_n(q)=[n]_q Φ_n(q)^2. First prove that the clearing factor U_{d,n}(q)=∏_{j=1}^{n-1}(1+q^{dj}) is coprime to M_n(q), so it will be invertible modulo the final modulus. Next rewrite the original theorem sum by using (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k=(q^d;q^d)_k(-q^d;q^d)_k, which replaces the denominator (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k by the correct denominator (-q^d;q^d)_k. Then show that each such denominator is coprime to M_n(q), so the rewritten sum and the target term both lie in the localization. After that, multiply the original difference by U_{d,n}(q); the denominator products cancel termwise, giving a Laurent polynomial G_{d,r,n}(q). The only theorem-specific input is the explicit bottleneck lemma asserting that G_{d,r,n}(q) is divisible by M_n(q) in Q[q,q^{-1}]. Unpack this divisibility as an equality U_{d,n}(q)(T_{d,r,n}(q)-R_{d,r,n}(q))=M_n(q)H_{d,r,n}(q) with H_{d,r,n}(q) Laurent. Finally use the generic localization lemma: since T_{d,r,n}(q) and R_{d,r,n}(q) lie in the localization and U_{d,n}(q) is invertible there because it is coprime to M_n(q), the cleared equality implies T_{d,r,n}(q) ≡ R_{d,r,n}(q) mod M_n(q). Unfolding the notation gives exactly the displayed theorem.

steps.derives: For admissible d,r,n, if M_n(q):=[n]_q Φ_n(q)^2 and U_{d,n}(q):=∏_{j=1}^{n-1}(1+q^{dj}), then gcd(U_{d,n}(q),M_n(q))=1 in Z[q].
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the conclusion of L1 after naming the final modulus M_n(q).

steps.derives: If A_{d,r,n,k}(q):=[3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2}/(-q^d;q^d)_k, then the original theorem sum T_{d,r,n}(q):=∑_{k=0}^{n-1} [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k^2 q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2}/(q^{2d};q^{2d})_k satisfies T_{d,r,n}(q)=∑_{k=0}^{n-1} A_{d,r,n,k}(q) in Q(q).
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the rewrite identity stated in L2.

steps.derives: With M_n(q):=[n]_q Φ_n(q)^2 and Loc_{M_n} the localization away from polynomials coprime to M_n(q), each A_{d,r,n,k}(q) belongs to Loc_{M_n}, the finite sum S_{d,r,n}(q):=∑_{k=0}^{n-1} A_{d,r,n,k}(q) belongs to Loc_{M_n}, and R_{d,r,n}(q):=[rn]_q q^{r(1-n)/2} belongs to Loc_{M_n}.
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the ambient-ring conclusion of L3.

steps.derives: The original theorem sum T_{d,r,n}(q) belongs to Loc_{M_n}, and the target term R_{d,r,n}(q) also belongs to Loc_{M_n}.
steps.trivial_justification: A2 identifies T_{d,r,n}(q) with the finite sum S_{d,r,n}(q) in Q(q). A3 states that S_{d,r,n}(q) lies in Loc_{M_n}. Therefore T_{d,r,n}(q) lies in Loc_{M_n}. A3 already gives R_{d,r,n}(q) ∈ Loc_{M_n}.

steps.derives: If G_{d,r,n}(q):=U_{d,n}(q)(T_{d,r,n}(q)-R_{d,r,n}(q)), then G_{d,r,n}(q) belongs to Z[q,q^{-1}].
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the cleared-polynomial statement of L4.

steps.derives: The Laurent polynomial G_{d,r,n}(q)=U_{d,n}(q)(T_{d,r,n}(q)-R_{d,r,n}(q)) is divisible by M_n(q)=[n]_q Φ_n(q)^2 in Q[q,q^{-1}].
steps.trivial_justification: This is precisely the bottleneck divisibility claim supplied by L5.

steps.derives: There exists H_{d,r,n}(q) in Q[q,q^{-1}] such that G_{d,r,n}(q)=M_n(q)H_{d,r,n}(q) in Q(q).
steps.trivial_justification: This is the definition of divisibility of G_{d,r,n}(q) by M_n(q) in the Laurent polynomial ring.

steps.derives: There exists H_{d,r,n}(q) in Q[q,q^{-1}] such that U_{d,n}(q)(T_{d,r,n}(q)-R_{d,r,n}(q))=M_n(q)H_{d,r,n}(q) in Q(q).
steps.trivial_justification: A5 defines G_{d,r,n}(q) as U_{d,n}(q)(T_{d,r,n}(q)-R_{d,r,n}(q)), and A7 states G_{d,r,n}(q)=M_n(q)H_{d,r,n}(q). Substituting the definition of G_{d,r,n}(q) yields the displayed cleared equality.

steps.derives: In the localized-congruence sense, T_{d,r,n}(q) ≡ R_{d,r,n}(q) mod M_n(q).
steps.trivial_justification: From A4, both T_{d,r,n}(q) and R_{d,r,n}(q) belong to Loc_{M_n}. From A1, the clearing factor U_{d,n}(q) is coprime to M_n(q). From A8, there exists H_{d,r,n}(q) in Q[q,q^{-1}] such that U_{d,n}(q)(T_{d,r,n}(q)-R_{d,r,n}(q))=M_n(q)H_{d,r,n}(q) in Q(q). These are exactly the hypotheses of L6 with M=M_n, U=U_{d,n}, X=T_{d,r,n}, and Y=R_{d,r,n}. Therefore L6 yields T_{d,r,n}(q) ≡ R_{d,r,n}(q) mod M_n(q).

steps.derives: Let [m]_q = (1−q^m)/(1−q), let (a;q)_k = ∏_{j=0}^{k−1} (1−aq^j), let (a,b,c;q)_k = (a;q)_k (b;q)_k (c;q)_k, and let Φ_n(q) be the nth cyclotomic polynomial. Prove that for positive integers d and r with gcd(d,r)=1 and r ≤ d, and for every integer n > 1 with n ≡ 1 mod 2d, we have ∑_{k=0}^{n−1} [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k^2 q^(k(d−dk−2r)/2) / (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k ≡ [rn]_q q^(r(1−n)/2) mod [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2.
steps.trivial_justification: A9 is exactly this statement after unfolding the definitions of T_{d,r,n}(q), R_{d,r,n}(q), and M_n(q), together with the standing notation for q-integers, q-shifted factorials, and congruence modulo M_n(q).
